context: Workers autonomously gather/build; explorers scout; warriors fight. Flags assign work or military attention, not direct unit movement.

entries.id: native:[Each colony's start is measured on the finished map: the walk to wheat and to wood, how well its ground regrows, the deposits and building sites within reach, and its distance from rivals. Every factor scores from 0 to 1 against a fixed bar, the total weighs them, fairness is the worst colony's total over the best, and the score is the worst total times the fairness.]

entries.source: Each colony's start is measured on the finished map: the walk to food and wood sources, how well its ground regrows, the deposits and building sites within reach, and its distance from rivals. Every factor scores from 0 to 1 against a fixed bar, the total weighs them, fairness is the worst colony's total over the best, and the score is the worst total times the fairness.
Tip: exploration flags send explorers to reveal the map; war flags gather your warriors.
Finished buildings the colony had. Split it to see each kind of building.
Buildings destroyed by enemies or demolished by the colony itself.
Buildings whose entrances were blocked, so units could not get in or out.

entries.id: native:[Units gain levels at training buildings and buildings can be upgraded. Repairs remain available when off.]
entries.key: [Units gain levels at training buildings and buildings can be upgraded. Repairs remain available when off.]
entries.source: Units gain levels at training buildings and buildings can be upgraded. Repairs remain available when off.

What the colony's workers were doing, moment by moment: working for a building, working at a flag, training, eating, healing, waiting hungry or hurt with no inn or hospital free, or idle with nothing to do. A healthy colony keeps most of its workers working, few idle and none waiting.
The share of workers' time spent with nothing to do. High values mean more workers than work; near zero means every worker is busy and jobs may be waiting.

How far hungry workers were, on average over their walk, from the inn they were heading for, in map squares in a straight line. A whole trip is roughly twice this. High values mean inns are far from where workers work.
How many warriors the colony had. Split it to see how many were near home, near an enemy colony, or in open ground. Ground close to both colonies counts as home.
The average attack level of the colony's warriors, counting attack speed and attack strength equally, on the 1 to 4 scale the game shows. Barracks raise it; new untrained warriors pull it down.
How the colony's warriors divided between those sent to a war flag, those hurt badly enough to leave the fight for a hospital (including those being healed), and those free.

Workers can fetch supplies from shared market stock. Markets can upgrade to store food and wood, then every material. Trading between teams remains fruit-only. Applies to new games; saves keep their original setting.

entries.source: No assigned Exploration Flag was found. Place one on the stone east of your base and request 1 explorer.
No assigned War Flag was found at the enemy base. Place one over the eastern enemy Swarm and request warriors.
Produce warriors at the Swarm, then train them at a Training Camp.
You controlled military production and trained warriors. Keep their food supply running; combat units still need to eat.

Set the Swarm to warriors only; assign suppliers and wait for 2 warriors. Set worker and explorer ratios to 0 and warrior ratio to 1. The Swarm consumes wheat for births. Ratios choose what is produced; suppliers determine whether it can run.
